_meta.note: General container-growing guidance for the prototype. Sun-hour bands and 'containers dry fast' guidance follow the cited extension sources. Stage day-ranges, container sizes and pot footprints are approximate planning values compiled for the prototype; they vary with variety, season and care, and must be verified by the Kisan Drishti team (e.g. against ICAR-IIHR / state agricultural university guidance) before release. Nutrient notes are what to watch for — not a diagnosis and never a dose.

items.name: Tomato

growing.focus: Steady leaf and root growth. Compost mixed into the potting mix carries the plant for the first weeks; heavy nitrogen now gives leaves instead of flowers.
watch: Pale older leaves — can mean low nitrogen
Purplish leaf undersides on young plants — often cold, sometimes low phosphorus

flowering.focus: Flowers and first fruit set. Keep moisture even and top-dress with compost or vermicompost.
watch: Flowers dropping — heat, a dry pot or uneven watering
Lots of leaf but few flowers — too much nitrogen

fruit.focus: Fruit filling. Even moisture matters most now; feed lightly with compost.
watch: Dark, sunken patch at the fruit's base (blossom-end rot) — linked to calcium reaching the fruit, usually from uneven watering
Scorched leaf edges — can mean low potassium

harvest.focus: Keep picking and keep feeding lightly so the plant sets more fruit.
watch: Cracked fruit — often a heavy watering after a dry spell

items.harvestNote: Pick when fully coloured and slightly soft.

items.name: Chilli

growing.focus: Build a sturdy bush. Compost in the mix; avoid over-feeding with nitrogen.
watch: Pale older leaves — can mean low nitrogen
Curled, crinkled leaves — check the undersides for mites, thrips or aphids

flowering.focus: Flowering. Even watering and a compost top-dress help flowers hold.
watch: Flowers dropping — very hot days or a pot that dried out

fruit.focus: Fruit filling. Keep moisture steady; feed lightly.
watch: Small, few fruit — too little sun is a common cause on shaded roofs

harvest.focus: Regular picking keeps the plant producing.
watch: Yellowing across the plant late in the season — feed lightly with compost

items.harvestNote: Pick green or let them turn red — both are ready.

items.name: Brinjal

growing.focus: Leaf and root growth. Compost in the mix is enough for now.
watch: Pale older leaves — can mean low nitrogen

flowering.focus: Flowering. Keep watering even; top-dress with compost.
watch: Flowers dropping — heat or a dry pot

fruit.focus: Fruit filling. Steady moisture and light feeding.
watch: Holes in shoots or fruit — check for shoot and fruit borer

harvest.focus: Pick often; the plant keeps fruiting for months with light feeding.
watch: Dull, seedy fruit — picked too late

items.harvestNote: Pick while the skin is still glossy.

items.name: Okra

growing.focus: Okra likes warmth. Compost in the mix; do not over-water young plants.
watch: Yellow veins on leaves — look for whiteflies (a sign of a virus spread by them)
Flowers dropping — a dry pot

fruit.focus: Pods grow fast — a few days from flower to pick.
watch: Tough pods — picked too late

harvest.focus: Pick every day or two; feed lightly with compost.
watch: Fewer pods — the plant needs picking and a little feeding

items.harvestNote: Pick small, tender pods every day or two.

items.name: Spinach

growing.focus: Leaf growth runs on nitrogen. Compost in the mix; keep the soil evenly moist.
watch: Evenly pale or yellow leaves — low nitrogen or a waterlogged pot

harvest.focus: Cut outer leaves and let the centre regrow; a thin compost top-dress after cutting helps.
watch: A tall central stalk (bolting) — heat makes palak flower early; afternoon shade delays it

items.harvestNote: Cut outer leaves; the centre keeps growing.

items.name: Fenugreek

growing.focus: Quick crop. Compost in the mix is usually enough.
watch: Pale, thin plants — sown too thickly or too little light

harvest.focus: Cut young shoots; resow every few weeks for a steady supply.
watch: Bitter, tough leaves — left too long

items.harvestNote: Cut young shoots; resow every few weeks.

growing.focus: Keep the soil evenly moist; compost in the mix.
watch: Yellowing — a waterlogged pot or too little light

harvest.focus: Cut leaves before flower stalks form; resow every few weeks.
watch: Flower stalks — heat makes dhaniya bolt; some shade helps

items.name: Mint

growing.focus: Roots spread fast — its own pot keeps it from taking over others.
watch: Leggy stems — too little light

harvest.focus: Pinch tops often to keep it bushy; top-dress with compost now and then.
watch: Small leaves — the pot is root-bound; divide and repot

items.harvestNote: Pinch the tops; it grows back.

insights.title: Tomatoes are the main source of lycopene
insights.body: Lycopene is a red carotenoid pigment. Researchers estimate about 80% of the lycopene in the US diet comes from tomatoes and tomato products.

insights.title: Clay pots need water more often
insights.body: Clay pots are porous, so water also evaporates through their sides. Small pots dry out faster than large ones.

insights.title: On a hot roof, check pots twice a day
insights.body: Containers on concrete in full sun dry very quickly. Feel the soil at least once a day, and twice on hot, dry or windy days.

insights.title: Greens grow with as little as 3 hours of sun
insights.body: Leafy greens tolerate shade far better than fruiting crops. Tomato and chilli need the most sun and warmth.

insights.title: A little shade keeps palak leafy for longer
insights.body: Crops that flower (bolt) quickly in hot weather, such as spinach and lettuce, keep growing longer with some shade.
